producer_report.summary: Added a `mistake` intervention category. Status and audit now count mistakes per class and per cause, apart from `interventions_by_category`, and show the prevention proposed for each cause. A mistake is category `mistake`, or a legacy `other` record whose text starts "Mistake:"; records are never rewritten. The cause comes from the recorded introspection, grouped by `normalise`. Mistakes with no recorded introspection count under "no cause recorded". Same-cause mistakes share one proposal, labelled check, knowledge or design change. Introspecting a mistake adds a `mistake_guidance` prompt key asking for the preventing check or knowledge. `athena audit` prints the mistake report before it runs the job audit, so the counts show when no audit is produced or the audit errors. Status prints mistakes only when there are some. `athena audit --json` is now one object with `mistakes`, a nullable `audit`, and a nullable `invocation`. README, CHANGELOG and athena-v0.md mention the category.

checks_run.note: Ran with -q after an earlier failing run that I fixed; every suite reported ok, 0 failed.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: new tests show an intervention logged with category `mistake` is accepted by the parser and appears in `InterventionCategory::ALL`, and an unknown category is still rejected with an error listing `mistake`.
criteria_check.evidence: records.rs `mistake_is_a_category_and_in_all` and `parse_accepts_mistake`; lifecycle.rs `intervene_accepts_mistake_and_rejects_unknown_category_listing_mistake`. All pass in `cargo test --locked`.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test with several mistake interventions of different classes and causes shows `athena status` output and its JSON report mistake counts per class and per cause, in fields separate from `interventions_by_category`.
criteria_check.evidence: lifecycle.rs `status_reports_mistakes_per_class_and_per_cause_apart_from_categories` (text, JSON through the binary, category counts unchanged) and introspection.rs `mistakes_with_the_same_cause_aggregate_into_one_proposal` (distinct causes in text and JSON). Both pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a CLI test in crates/athena-cli/tests (auditor.rs or introspection.rs) runs the audit command and asserts its output reports mistakes per class and per cause. A second case asserts the mistake counts still print when no job audit is produced.
criteria_check.evidence: auditor.rs `the_audit_output_reports_mistakes_per_class_and_per_cause` (audit Some) and `the_audit_output_reports_mistakes_when_no_audit_is_produced` (nested, None). introspection.rs `athena_audit_prints_mistakes_before_any_audit` runs the real `athena audit` and `athena audit --json` with no job, where the audit errors, and asserts stdout. All pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test shows that introspecting a `mistake` intervention yields a proposal naming the check or knowledge that would have prevented it, and that mistakes with the same cause aggregate into one proposal.
criteria_check.evidence: introspection.rs `a_mistake_intervention_is_introspected_with_guidance_for_the_preventing_check_or_knowledge` (guidance key on mistake and legacy prompts, absent on an ordinary one, proposal kind `check` and prevention text) and `mistakes_with_the_same_cause_aggregate_into_one_proposal` (3 mistakes, 2 proposals, the shared one covers 2). status.rs unit test covers the kind mapping.

criteria_check.criterion: Existing records with category `other` and text starting 'Mistake:' are counted as mistakes in status and the audit. Records are not rewritten. The text-prefix rule is documented in a code comment or doc.
criteria_check.evidence: lifecycle.rs `a_legacy_other_record_starting_mistake_colon_is_counted_in_status_and_audit_and_not_rewritten` (the stored file is byte-identical and still says `other`); status.rs unit test of the same name prefix; records.rs `is_mistake_rule`. The rule is in the `is_mistake` doc comment and in athena-v0.md.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean, and `cargo test` passes in full.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` printed no diagnostics. `cargo test --locked -q` showed every suite ok.

criteria_check.criterion: Outcome-check: a reader of the status or audit output can see how many mistakes occurred, which classes and causes recur, and which prevention work was proposed. README.md, CHANGELOG.md and the category list in docs/design/athena-v0.md mention the `mistake` category.
criteria_check.evidence: Asserted output lines: `mistakes N: by class: ...`, `mistakes by cause: ...`, and `prevention (kind, n mistake(s)): ...`. lifecycle.rs `the_readme_changelog_and_design_name_the_mistake_category` checks the three docs. The fresh-reader rating is prose-only and I did not do it.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: manage.rs and reading.rs are unedited; neither needed a change. The named test `intervene_accepts_mistake_and_rejects_unknown_category_listing_mistake` is in lifecycle.rs, because manage.rs unit tests have no repository fixture.

Departure from the plan: `display::audit_report` takes the mistake report and an optional audit. On the audit error path, main.rs prints the mistake report itself (text or JSON) and then returns the error. I did not make a `display::audit_report(report, Option)` call in both paths.

The binary audit test uses a job-less repository, where the audit errors. I did not exercise `athena audit` under ATHENA_NESTED in the binary. The nested None case is covered by the library test in auditor.rs.
Causes group only when their normalised text is equal. Grouping by failure class instead is a product choice I left open.
I did not do the fresh-reader rating (outcome-check). It is prose-only.
mistakes: My first integration tests called `introspect_intervention` after `intervene`, which had already introspected. Tests consumed scripted replies in the wrong order and failed. I fixed this.
My status.rs unit tests first failed clippy (`field_reassign_with_default`). I fixed this by allowing the lint on the test module.
learnings: `Athena::intervene` already runs `introspect_intervention` itself, so a test that scripts model replies must not call it again.
`Records` implements `Default`; clippy's `field_reassign_with_default` fires on it in unit tests unless allowed.
In a repository with no job, `athena audit` errors in the binary. The mistake report is printed on that error path.
`PreventionKind` has no 'knowledge' value. I map `Default` to knowledge and `CodeCheck` to check in the report.
desires: The Bash tool allows no pipes or tail, so large test output could not be trimmed or searched. Only `-q` made it readable.
